sections.what_happened: Algeria's Council of the Nation (upper house) voted on Sunday to approve a presidential decision deploying a People's National Army detachment to Niger to secure oil projects belonging to state energy company Sonatrach. AFP's anonymous senator put the vote at 148 of 174 in favour; Anadolu reported it as unanimous. The People's National Assembly (lower house) was due to vote later Sunday evening; Article 91 of the constitution requires a two-thirds majority in each chamber. If deployed, it would be Algeria's first military mission abroad since the 1973 Arab-Israeli war. Context: Niger defence minister Gen. Salifou Modi visited Algiers last week and signed an undisclosed military-cooperation protocol; in late August Algeria sent four Su-30 jets (two patrols) plus a refuelling aircraft to Niamey at Niger's request after an alleged coup attempt; President Tebboune said Oct 3: 'We will protect Niger no matter what.'
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct publisher families agree on the vote and its purpose; vote-count wording differs (148/174 vs unanimous).
sections.what_disputed: Vote-count discrepancy: AFP (via Al Arabiya/EWN) reports 148 of 174 in favour; Anadolu (via TRT Afrika/Saudi Gazette) reports a unanimous vote. No official vote tally published yet. The deployment itself is still pending the lower-house vote, so 'deployment approved' is not yet final.
sections.why_matters: First time since 1973: Algeria votes to send troops abroad — not to fight a war, but to guard oil in Niger. The vote passed the upper house; the lower house votes tonight, and the Arab internet is already split between protection and entanglement.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (vote Sunday, missed by the 1700 scan) -- Algeria's upper house votes to deploy troops to Niger to guard Sonatrach oil facilities; first foreign deployment since 1973; lower-house vote due Sunday evening

totw_analysis: Our read: First time since 1973: Algeria votes to send troops abroad — not to fight a war, but to guard oil in Niger. The vote passed the upper house; the lower house votes tonight, and the Arab internet is already split between protection and entanglement. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Protection of Algeria's southern border and Sonatrach interests vs entanglement in a Sahel proxy war at the cost of Algerian soldiers' lives — Arabic-language comment threads split between patriotic support and warnings about cost, casualties and constitutional legitimacy.
